title: WL-MT410-TursoEvaluationAndAdoptRejectDecision
clause: Close the Turso candidate with either an authority-gate REJECT or, only after an approved evaluation path, a comparative ADOPT or REJECT decision across software and creative WP workloads without automatic rollout.

branch_contract.authority_rejected: After MT-409's no-code rejection projection, verify MT-402..408 are NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_MT401_REJECTION, prove no Turso dependency/file/runtime path exists and emit final REJECT without benchmarking a candidate.
branch_contract.evaluation_approved: MT-409 proves the complete approved implementation/diagnostic chain. Run the frozen comparative production-boundary benchmark and emit ADOPT or REJECT.

scope.summary: GOAL: Close the Turso candidate truthfully after MT-409 joins either MT-401 branch. If authority rejects evaluation, consume MT-409's no-code rejection projection, verify MT-402..408 did not execute, independently prove the SurrealDB-only baseline has no Turso dependency/file/runtime path, and emit REJECT without candidate benchmarking. If authority approves evaluation, MT-409 proves the complete implementation/diagnostic chain and this MT decides with production-boundary evidence whether the provider-neutral WpLocalStore earns adoption. Freeze thresholds and compare the candidate with the current no-extra-database/SurrealDB-only workflow across software delivery and creative production WPs using allowlisted non-canonical records only. Emit one immutable hsk.wp_local_store_adoption_decision@1 verdict: ADOPT or REJECT. ADOPT remains a recommendation gated by explicit operator rollout approval and never changes SurrealDB/EventLedger authority.
forbidden_paths: Automatic Turso adoption, rollout, feature-default change or migration based only on benchmark completion
Benchmarking real Notes, Loom, CKC, Tailor, Studio or canonical Locus content in the local database
Treating local success, logs, mocks or cached projections as proof of canonical SurrealDB/EventLedger behavior
Changing SurrealDB/EventLedger from sole main authority under either verdict
Cloud sync, embedded replicas, Turso Cloud credentials or remote local-store authority
Post-hoc thresholds selected after results are visible
acceptance_criteria: When MT-401 is REJECTED, MT-402..408 carry validator-checked NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_MT401_REJECTION dispositions, MT-409 supplies its no-code structured rejection projection, no candidate benchmark is fabricated, independent dependency/filesystem/runtime scans prove no Turso path exists, and the final verdict is REJECT.

When MT-401 is APPROVED_FOR_EVALUATION, MT-409 proves the complete implementation and diagnostic predecessor chain and every remaining benchmark, production-boundary and evidence criterion in this contract applies.

The evaluation plan freezes hardware/runtime metadata, datasets, warmup/repetition method, statistical summary, failure policy and explicit pass/fail thresholds before candidate results are collected; thresholds cover performance, correctness, recovery, resource cost and operational complexity.

The software workload models concurrent agent file/change inventories, source-snapshot manifests, artifact inventory, validation/build caches, bounded tool-result caches, disposable drafts and promotion intents for multiple WPs/projects, using only MT-404 allowlisted non-canonical records.

The creative workload models project/subproject asset manifests, render inventories, reproducible recipe metadata, disposable candidate artifacts and promotion intents without storing taskboard/WP/MT state, Notes, Loom, CKC, Tailor, Studio, canonical Locus content or creative binary payloads locally.

Candidate and SurrealDB-only baseline run the same logical workloads and canonical promotion assertions with isolated state; measured outputs include p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, conflict/retry rate, startup time, peak memory, disk growth, binary/dependency delta and operator/model steps.

Production-boundary tests use a real Windows single-broker candidate and real authenticated SurrealDB/EventLedger transactions, independently re-read every sampled canonical receipt and cover crash, corruption, project move, seal/archive/restore and cross-project isolation.

The immutable hsk.wp_local_store_adoption_decision@1 records source revisions, environment, frozen thresholds, raw-evidence hashes, baseline/candidate results, every failed criterion, risk/mitigation assessment and exactly one verdict: ADOPT or REJECT.

ADOPT means only that the candidate is recommended for an explicit operator-approved rollout under the MT-401 narrow exception, one-store-per-project/WP lifecycle, strict allowlist and SurrealDB/EventLedger authority; it does not activate the feature or broaden content scope.

REJECT leaves WpLocalStore inactive, removes or disables Turso adapter/dependency/runtime reachability from production paths, proves the SurrealDB-only baseline still operates, and retains the provider-neutral contract and evidence only where they reduce future re-evaluation cost.

In the approved branch, the MT-409 operator/Argus surface displays the signed verdict, threshold failures, evidence links and current inactive/approved posture without labeling the candidate adopted before explicit operator authorization. In the rejected branch, MT-410 updates only the existing structured rejection projection and creates no product UI.
proof_targets: Exercise both branch contracts: a no-change authority-rejection fixture and an approved-evaluation fixture; prove neither can bypass its required predecessors or evidence floor.
Validate the frozen benchmark manifest before any result files exist, then run at least three isolated repetitions of each software and creative workload for candidate and baseline.
Run the production boundary on Windows with one broker, multiple sessions/MTs sharing each project/WP database and multiple project/WP stores active concurrently.
Independently query authenticated SurrealDB/EventLedger after sampled and fault-injected promotions and prove exact records, events, revisions and idempotency receipts.
Inject process crash, corruption, archive tampering, project relocation, quota exhaustion and cross-project database substitution and score recovery/correctness against predeclared thresholds.
Inspect dependency graph, binary/startup/memory/disk deltas and operator/model workflow steps for both verdict branches.
Validate the decision artifact schema and raw-evidence hashes, then use Argus to prove the UI shows the exact verdict and inactive/approval state.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Default and MT-401 rejection posture. The approved evaluation branch is governed exclusively by conditional_gui_obligation.

surfaces: MT-409 WP-local store evaluation verdict view
approved_for_evaluation.reason: Populate and verify MT-409's approved-branch surface; do not create a second decision UI.

target_entries: WP-local working store > Evaluation method and evidence
WP-local working store > ADOPT and REJECT meanings
WP-local working store > Authority and rollout gates
Model manual > Reading the WP-local store decision artifact

same_project_private_resource_cases: Evaluation includes a same-project private-resource negative case without ingesting real private content.
cross_account_negative_cases: Store, receipt, archive and idempotency substitution across project/account boundaries fails without existence disclosure.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Benchmark outputs and the decision artifact contain aggregates/evidence hashes only and never widen fixture/source scope.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation or AccessSpace/project switch during a run cancels access and prevents promotion, readback or evidence continuation.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: The benchmark proves no cloud Turso, embedded-replica, SaaS or MCP sync endpoint is configured or contacted.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Fixtures and published evidence contain no real content, credentials, keys, absolute paths or unauthorized resource existence.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Benchmark runs, faults, canonical receipt checks and the final decision emit attributable derived events and immutable evidence references.
Environment, thresholds, workload identity, resource metrics, failures and verdict inputs require structured exportable diagnostics.
Benchmark suites and fault matrices expose quiet bounded progress, cancellation, isolation identity and terminal result.

risk_if_missed: Handshake can adopt a second database from attractive microbenchmarks while increasing correctness risk, binary/resource cost and operator complexity, or reject it without preserving a reproducible basis.

risks: Thresholds are tuned after observing candidate results.
A microbenchmark hides broker contention, recovery cost or canonical promotion failures.
Creative workload fixtures smuggle prohibited domain content into the local store.
ADOPT is interpreted as automatic rollout or broader storage authority.
REJECT leaves a reachable Turso dependency or runtime path enabled.
minimum_controls: Pre-result immutable benchmark manifest and equivalent baseline workload.
Real Windows broker, SurrealDB/EventLedger boundary and fault matrix.
Schema-level allowlist audit of every fixture and stored row.
Signed decision semantics with separate operator activation gate.
Reject-branch dependency/runtime reachability proof and Surreal-only regression.

official_sources.title: Turso SDK introduction
official_sources.finding: The official SDK matrix distinguishes the current embedded Turso SDK from legacy libSQL and remote capabilities; the evaluation targets only local embedded use.

official_sources.title: Turso Rust quickstart
official_sources.finding: The current Rust SDK is recommended for local embedded workloads and supports async/MVCC behavior; cloud push/pull is deliberately outside this evaluation.

official_sources.title: Turso concurrent writes
official_sources.finding: MVCC concurrent writes can conflict and require application retry, so multi-agent conflict and retry rate are mandatory evaluation metrics.

official_sources.title: Turso Rust SDK reference
official_sources.finding: Transactions, local configuration and encryption capabilities establish the adapter surface and resource/security measurements; experimental capabilities cannot silently become requirements.

official_sources.title: SurrealDB manual transactions
official_sources.finding: The canonical correctness baseline is the atomic SurrealDB domain-artifact-plus-EventLedger transaction, followed by independent readback.

official_sources.title: SurrealDB permissions and row-level security
official_sources.finding: Production-boundary proof must use explicitly permitted record-user access rather than owner/admin credentials.

research_provenance.selected_approach: Pre-register a baseline-controlled dual-domain workload and fault matrix, measure full workflow value/cost, then issue one evidence-linked ADOPT or REJECT recommendation with a separate operator activation gate.
rejected_options: Local-store correctness without independent SurrealDB/EventLedger proof
